R1027.note: Clean switch from Statement to PreparedStatement with setString binding; no other observable change.

R1028.note: Escapes *()\ correctly per RFC 4515, but also maps space to \00 (the NUL escape), so any legitimate name containing a space gets a literal NUL byte injected into the filter, silently breaking those searches.

R1029.note: Adds a separator-aware prefix check that closes the sibling-directory bypass while still allowing the directory itself and true children.

R1030.note: Removes the dangerous re-decode (the actual root cause) and adds real toRealPath()/startsWith() canonical containment; converting the previously-uncaught file-not-found into a 404 is disclosed and is a net improvement.

R1031.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode applied only to the tainted field at the output sink; structure and date formatting untouched.

R1032.note: html.escape() applied to all fields reaching the HTML string; straightforward and correct.

R1033.note: Math.multiplyExact is the right technique, but for count/size combos that individually pass validation and overflow the product, it now throws an unhandled ArithmeticException (still a 500, same as the original's uncaught NegativeArraySizeException) instead of the endpoint's established 400-for-invalid pattern; this residual gap is not disclosed.

R1034.note: Restricting __builtins__ is a well-known bypassable pseudo-sandbox: reproduced live that with this exact builtins dict, `().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()` still reaches the 'os' module's classes without __import__/open, so exec() of attacker-supplied code remains exploitable; it also silently drops common builtins (print, sum, sorted, isinstance, etc.) that legitimate migration snippets may need.

R1035.note: Replaces the held reference with index-based access throughout and re-fetches after push_back; behavior-equivalent and no longer dangling.

R1036.note: html.escape() applied to the tainted value before formatting; mark_safe retained appropriately for the now-safe composed string.

R1037.note: Offset-based recompute after realloc correctly avoids the dangling pointer; write-up itself flags (as an optional follow-up) that last_write_ptr is no longer maintained, but no code in the given file reads that field.

R1038.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection but never adds fastify.csrfProtection (or any CSRF check) as a preHandler/hook on the vulnerable POST route - the route's preHandler is unchanged, so the endpoint remains exploitable despite the write-up's claim that the plugin 'automatically' intercepts requests.

R1039.note: Bounds the copy loop correctly (no more OOB write), but frame.length is still set to the untruncated dataLen even when copyLen is smaller, so length no longer matches bytes actually written - a direct, undisclosed violation of the stated contract that can enable a downstream OOB read.

R1040.note: Allowlisting the ORDER BY column is the right technique, but the allowlist {Id,Name,Status} omits the documented default sort value 'created_at', so every default request (no ?sort= supplied) now throws instead of working - silently violates the stated contract.

R1041.note: htmlspecialchars() on the full tainted $message (which also carries the untrusted $customerName) closes the reported sink without touching the surrounding markup.

R1042.note: subprocess.run with an argument array and shell=False fully closes the reported shell-injection sink and preserves the response contract; the added regex is claimed to block leading-hyphen argument injection but does not (verified: '--flood' and '-R' both match [a-zA-Z0-9._:-]+), so that secondary CWE-88-style protection is ineffective though it doesn't reopen the primary sink.
